questions.q: What exercise does the summary recommend for finding your calling?
a: List the major events in your life and look for moments of fulfilment
Write down your five greatest skills and rank them
Ask friends what job they think suits you
Track how you spend every hour for a month
questions.why: Lesson 1 suggests listing major life events, then asking when you felt happiest and most fulfilled.

questions.q: What questions does the summary suggest asking as you review your list of life events?
a: When was I happiest, most fulfilled and most accomplished
Which events earned me the most money and status
Which events would other people find most impressive
Which events took the longest to recover from
questions.why: Lesson 1 says your calling hides in the moments when you felt happy, fulfilled and accomplished.

questions.q: Why does the summary reject the idea of being self-made?
a: Even the greatest people relied on teachers, mentors and coaches
Success depends mostly on luck and timing
Millionaires usually inherit their money
Everyone needs a formal university degree
questions.why: Lesson 2 cites Buffett, Jordan and Bezos to show that no one succeeds without help.

Holding several jobs at once to earn more income
Investing in a mix of stocks and bonds
Planning your career in five-year stages
questions.why: Lesson 3 defines a portfolio life as building identity from a wide range of things.

questions.q: Which four areas does Jeff say a portfolio life includes?
a: Work, home, play and purpose
Work, health, wealth and community
Career, family, faith and service
Work, rest, learning and giving
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists work alongside home, play and purpose as the parts of a full life.
